claim: § The Seventeen Symmetries and § The Prism Machine Principle: "exactly 17 ways"; the crystallographic restriction forbids 5-fold rotation ("you'll either leave gaps or create overlaps"); a single fundamental domain plus group operations generates every periodic pattern. The text describes a kaleidoscope it cannot spin.

pieces.what: Starts from one motif tile and translation only (p1), then adds one operation at a time (2-fold, mirror, glide, 3-, 4-, 6-fold) to reach all 17, naming each group as it forms

Lets the reader try 5-fold rotation on a lattice and watch the gaps open, testing the crystallographic restriction; the same piece lists the 17 by family and will show the page's own count breakdown ('4 with no symmetry except translation') does not add up
pieces.walks_up_from: a square lattice with a 4-fold centre

pieces.section: Musical Symmetry: Rhythm as Wallpaper Group
pieces.what: A 16-step sequencer that plays a cell under translation, reversal and shift, and tests the 'rhythmic impossibility theorem' sentence against what a 1D timeline can actually hold
